title: "Audit of incomplete concomitant Huber paths"

# Scope

This audit addresses the first failed penalty in each of seven ROME-validation
paths. It preserves the historical 2000-sweep results and uses their saved
coefficient vectors and scales as initial states. It does not rerun or rank
whole paths. Diagnostic state recording and independent optimization are
excluded from timing comparisons.

Run python analysis/audit_incomplete_paths.py. All numerical results below
come from package coordinate/MM kernels; each instrumented continuation must
reproduce an ordinary production warm solve to $10^{-13}$.

# Independent objective bounds

For
$$
F(\beta,\sigma)=\frac1n\sum_i\sigma h_\rho((y_i-X_i^\top\beta)/\sigma)
+a\sigma+\lambda_0\|\beta\|_1,
$$
the closed perspective has the dual
$$
\sup_{v\in\mathbb R^n}\frac{y^\top v}{n}
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
\|v\|_\infty\le\rho,\qquad
\|X^\top v/n\|_\infty\le\lambda_0,\qquad
\frac{\|v\|_2^2}{2n}\le a .
$$
Indeed, $h_\rho^*(v)=v^2/2+\iota_{[-\rho,\rho]}(v)$; minimizing
the coefficient and nonnegative scale blocks gives the last two constraints.
Every feasible $v$ supplies a lower bound, independently of a dual optimizer's
success flag. We solve this smooth constrained problem with SLSQP and rescale
its returned vector into feasibility with a small inward numerical margin.
One SLSQP run reports a line-search failure; its feasible rescaled vector is
retained and still supplies a tight lower bound. These are floating-point
feasibility checks, not interval-arithmetic certificates.

The boundary problem is independently solved by a HiGHS linear program:
$$
F_{\partial}=\min_\beta
\frac{\rho}{n}\|y-X\beta\|_1+\lambda_0\|\beta\|_1.
$$
The LP dual multipliers are also rescaled into feasibility. At every audited
point, their lower bound exceeds the objective of the saved positive-scale
iterate. Subject to floating-point feasibility accuracy, this excludes
a global zero-scale solution at that penalty.

# Controlled continuations

The main continuation uses the unchanged batch size $B=8$, tolerance
$10^{-6}$ and a prespecified budget of 4000 **additional** sweeps. Diagnostic
variants use $B=1$, $B=64$, or freeze scale at its saved value, each with 2000
additional sweeps. There is no iterative budget search. Frozen-scale convergence
certifies its coefficient block only; its scale score need not vanish.

{{< include outputs/incomplete-path-audit/results.qmd >}}

All seven main continuations satisfy the original joint stopping test.
The $B=64$ sweep counts equal the $B=8$ counts in all seven cases. The $B=1$
counts differ by only two sweeps in one case. Freezing scale still requires
44--1645 coefficient sweeps.

The original primal-minus-dual bounds range from approximately
$5.5\times10^{-11}$ to $1.4\times10^{-7}$, despite coefficient KKT residuals
above $10^{-6}$. Final main-continuation gaps are below $3\times10^{-10}$.
Recomputed residuals reproduce the kernel's coefficient scores to within
$5\times10^{-14}$, providing no evidence of consequential residual drift.

# Local conditioning

With active coordinates $A$ and central residuals
$I=\{i:|r_i|<\rho\sigma\}$, away from kinks and sign changes the smooth
joint Hessian is
$$
H=\frac1{n\sigma}\sum_{i\in I}
\begin{pmatrix}X_{i,A}\\ r_i/\sigma\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}X_{i,A}\\ r_i/\sigma\end{pmatrix}^{\!\top}.
$$
It has full local rank at all seven saved points, with numerical condition
numbers approximately $8.9\times10^3$ to $5.5\times10^5$. Both Block-AR cases
have only two active coefficients; the largest predictor RMS ratio exceeds
100. Thus active-set size alone does not explain sweep counts.

The local Jacobian of a scale-MM step is
$M_\sigma=I-\{\sigma/(2a)\}e_\sigma e_\sigma^\top H$.
For exact coefficient coordinate $j$,
$M_j=I-e_je_j^\top H/H_{jj}$.
The idealized full-sweep map with $B$ scale steps has Jacobian
$$
M_A\cdots M_1M_\sigma^B.
$$
Its spectral radius is approximately $0.995$--$0.999$ for $B=8$ at the
saved states. These are local diagnostics on the current smooth branch:
active sets and Huber regions may change, and early stopping of a scale
batch changes the realized map. They are not a global convergence theorem.

![Scale, objective bound, and coefficient stationarity during additional sweeps. Frozen scale solves a different restricted problem and is a diagnostic only.](outputs/incomplete-path-audit/diagnostics.png)

# Implication

The evidence identifies slow coefficient convergence under a strict absolute
stationarity criterion at these seven points. More scale updates are not the
appropriate remedy. An objective-preserving acceleration of correlated active
coordinates is the next solver experiment; compare it against the unchanged
cyclic baseline with identical objective and joint accuracy checks. Do not
weaken the historical gates or infer completion of the remaining path tails.

The fixed-scale comparison and the unconstrained c-lasso R4 comparison remain
equally important. This audit changes neither comparator nor the timing results.
